rounds.question:
Interview round 1. Read the current context and identify its marker. Explain the approach, invariant, and boundary cases for solve(nums1, nums2). Do not implement yet.
Use only the current application attachments; earlier tasks are historical. Identify the exact current marker from the attachment.
rounds.answer:
The exact current marker is INTERVIEW-1-0b496e4637aec246. The screen asks for JavaScript solve(nums1, nums2) to return the median of two ascending arrays with positive combined length, targeting O(log(m+n)); no stdin/stdout, imports, or exports.

Approach: binary-search the shorter array. If its cut is i, choose the other cut j so i+j=floor((m+n+1)/2). Compare the values immediately left and right of both cuts.

Invariant: the left side always contains half the total elements, rounded up, and the search interval retains a valid partition. A partition is valid when left1≤right2 and left2≤right1; because each array is sorted, these checks ensure every left-side value is at most every right-side value. If left1>right2, move i left; if left2>right1, move i right.

At a valid partition, an odd total returns the larger left boundary; an even total returns the average of the larger left boundary and smaller right boundary. Treat missing left boundaries as −Infinity and missing right boundaries as +Infinity. This handles one empty array, a single combined element, cuts at either endpoint, duplicates, negative values, and completely separated value ranges; both arrays empty is excluded by the contract.

Time is O(log(min(m,n)+1)), with O(1) extra space. No implementation yet.
